```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import pickle
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "../code/python")
from run_analysis import make_length_figure

results_path = Path("../output/results.pkl")
with results_path.open("rb") as results_file:
    results = pickle.load(results_file)

annual_table = results["annual_table"]
annual_data = results["annual_data"]
highlights = results["highlights"]


def convert_gt_to_latex(gt_table):
    latex_str = gt_table.as_latex()
    lines = latex_str.split('\n')
    processed = []
    for line in lines:
        if any(s in line for s in ['\\begin{table}', '\\end{table}',
                                    '\\fontsize', '\\selectfont', '\\caption*']):
            continue
        line = line.replace('{tabular*}', '{tabular}')
        line = line.replace('{1.0\\linewidth}{@{\\extracolsep{\\fill}}', '{')
        line = line.replace('{\\linewidth}{@{\\extracolsep{\\fill}}', '{')
        processed.append(line)
    return processed
```

\pagebreak

# Introduction

@DLS2017 study the development of 10-K filings over their sample period of 1996 to 2013 and document that the length of the documents increases significantly over time. Using filing metadata from the EDGAR 10-K dataset, I replicate their trend figure and extend the analysis to 2023.

# Procedure

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(
    f"Filing metadata comes from the EDGAR 10-K dataset maintained by the TRR266 server, "
    f"accessed via DuckDB over HTTPS. I restrict the sample to filings with successful "
    f"markdown conversion and at least 3,000 words, keep one filing per firm per calendar "
    f"year (the most recent), and require a filing date between 1995 and 2023. "
    f"The final sample contains {highlights['sample_size']:,} firm-year observations from "
    f"{highlights['n_firms']:,} unique firms spanning {highlights['year_range']}."
)
```

# Results

```{python}
#| label: fig-length
#| fig-cap: "10-K word count over time. Each point represents the median word count across all firm-year observations in that calendar year."
#| out-width: 85%
make_length_figure(annual_data).draw()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-annual
#| tbl-cap: "Annual summary of 10-K filing characteristics."
#| output: asis
latex_lines = convert_gt_to_latex(annual_table)
print("\n".join([
    "\\begin{threeparttable}",
    "\n".join(l for l in latex_lines if l.strip()),
    "\\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]",
    "\\setlength{\\labelsep}{0pt}",
    "\\item \\emph{Note}: Sample restricted to 10-K filings with $\\geq$ 3,000 words "
    "and successful markdown conversion, one per firm per calendar year.",
    "\\end{tablenotes}",
    "\\end{threeparttable}",
]))
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
change = highlights["median_words_last"] - highlights["median_words_first"]
pct = round(100 * change / highlights["median_words_first"])
first_year, last_year = highlights["year_range"].split("–")
print(
    f"@fig-length shows that the time trend documented by @DLS2017 continues beyond their "
    f"sample period. Median word count rose from {highlights['median_words_first']:,} words "
    f"in {first_year} to {highlights['median_words_last']:,} words in {last_year}, "
    f"an increase of approximately {pct} percent."
)
```

# Conclusion

Replication using a different data source and extended sample period confirms the main finding of @DLS2017: 10-K filings continue to grow longer over time.
